scenario: Verify Successful Login With Valid Credentials
steps:
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Enter a valid admin username and password
3. Click Login
input: Admin / admin123 (OrangeHRM's published public-demo login; env-overridable)
expected: User is redirected to the Dashboard; breadcrumb reads "Dashboard"

scenario: Verify Navigation To Admin Page From Side Panel
steps:
1. Log in
2. Click "Admin" in the side panel
expected: Admin page loads; breadcrumb reads "Admin"

scenario: Add Employee Without Middle Name
steps:
1. Log in
2. Navigate to PIM
3. Click Add
4. Fill First Name, Last Name, and Employee Id
5. Click Save
input: Faker-generated unique first/last name; generated Employee Id suffix
expected: Employee is created; the new Personal Details page shows the entered first and last name
notes: Created via the UI (it is the subject); tracked marker id, deleted by teardown. Waits for the save redirect.

scenario: Add Employee With Middle Name
steps:
1. Log in
2. Navigate to PIM
3. Click Add
4. Fill First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, and Employee Id
5. Click Save
input: Faker-generated unique first/middle/last name; generated Employee Id suffix
expected: Employee is created; the new Personal Details page shows the entered first and last name
notes: Created via the UI (it is the subject); tracked marker id, deleted by teardown. Waits for the save redirect.

scenario: Create Employee With Enabled Login Credentials
steps:
1. Add a new employee
2. Toggle "Create Login Details"
3. Enter a username and password
4. Set status to Enabled
5. Save
6. Log out
7. Log back in as the new user
input: Faker-generated unique name, username, and password
expected: The new user logs in successfully and their own profile name is visible
notes: Password always contains a digit (the form silently refuses one without). Employee and user deleted by teardown (deleting the employee removes the user).

scenario: Create Employee With Disabled Login Credentials
steps:
1. Add a new employee
2. Toggle "Create Login Details"
3. Enter a username and password
4. Set status to Disabled
5. Save
6. Log out
7. Attempt to log in as the new user
input: Faker-generated unique name, username, and password
expected: Login is rejected with an "Account disabled" message
notes: Same as TC_CEF_003: digit in the password, employee and user deleted by teardown.

scenario: Add Employee Shows Required Field Errors When Name Is Blank
steps:
1. Log in
2. Navigate to PIM > Add Employee
3. Leave First Name and Last Name blank
4. Click Save
expected: A "Required" validation message appears under both First Name and Last Name
notes: Soft assertions for the two field errors; creates no data, so nothing to clean up

scenario: Cancel Add Employee Returns To Employee List
steps:
1. Log in
2. Navigate to PIM > Add Employee
3. Click Cancel
expected: User is returned to the Employee List (the "Add" button is visible again)
notes: Creates no data

scenario: Edit Employee Name Fields
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Open that employee's Personal Details page
3. Edit First Name and Last Name
4. Click Save
5. Reload the page
input: Faker-generated unique name for creation; edited values prefixed "Edited"
expected: "Successfully Updated" toast appears; the reloaded page shows the edited name
notes: Employee created via the API and deleted by teardown. Waits for network idle before editing (the form re-populates after load).

scenario: Search Employee By Name Shows Matching Result
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Navigate to PIM Employee List
3. Search by the employee's last name
input: Faker-generated unique last name (single word, for a reliable autocomplete match)
expected: Exactly one row matching the searched employee is shown
notes: Employee created via the API and deleted by teardown. Last name has a random suffix so "exactly one match" holds on a list of hundreds.

scenario: Delete Employee
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Search for them by last name in the Employee List
3. Click the row's delete icon
4. Confirm "Yes, Delete"
5. Navigate directly to the employee's (former) Personal Details URL
expected: "Successfully Deleted" toast appears; the employee's URL now shows "No Records Found"
notes: Only ever deletes the employee it created. Teardown then finds nothing left, which proves cleanup is safe on already-deleted data.

scenario: A Generated Employee Id Is Valid, Recognised As Ours, And Fresh
steps:
1. Generate an Employee Id
2. Check its length, whether it is recognised as a test id, and whether it is stale
expected: Exactly 10 characters (the server limit), recognised as ours, not stale
notes: No browser or network

scenario: An Id Becomes Stale Exactly At The Age Threshold, Not Before
steps:
1. Generate ids stamped just under and exactly at the stale threshold
2. Check staleness of each
expected: Just under the threshold: not stale. Exactly at it: stale.
notes: Boundary test of the purge's age rule

scenario: Ids That Are Not Ours Are Never Recognised
steps: 1. Check ordinary ids, empty/null ids, wrong-length ids, wrong-case prefixes, and ids with the prefix not at the start
expected: None is treated as a test id or as stale
notes: Guards against deleting other people's data

scenario: Generated Ids Are Unique
steps: 1. Generate 500 ids within the same time unit
expected: All 500 are distinct

scenario: An Id Stamped In The Future Is Never Treated As Stale
steps:
1. Generate an id stamped in the future
2. Check staleness
expected: Recognised as a test id but never stale (clock skew, or not ours - leave it)

scenario: Purge Deletes Only Stale Test Employees
steps:
1. Fake store holds a stale test employee, a fresh one, someone else's, a look-alike name containing QAR, and one with no id
2. Run the purge
expected: Only the stale test employee is deleted; everything else survives
notes: Mutation-checked: trusting the server's substring match makes this fail

scenario: Purge Refuses To Delete Anything When There Are Suspiciously Many Matches
steps:
1. Fake store holds more stale test employees than the safety cap
2. Run the purge
expected: Nothing is deleted and the refusal is reported
notes: Mutation-checked: removing the cap makes this fail

scenario: Cleanup Deletes Only What This Test Created
steps:
1. Create an employee through TestData; the store also holds another run's marked employee and someone else's
2. Run cleanup
expected: Only this test's employee is deleted

scenario: Cleanup Is Safe When There Is Nothing To Delete, And Safe To Run Twice
steps:
1. Issue an id that is never used and create one employee
2. Run cleanup twice
expected: First run deletes one; second deletes none; nothing throws
notes: Covers a test that fails before saving, and a test that already deleted its own data

scenario: A Failing Cleanup Never Throws, And Reports What It Could Not Remove
steps:
1. Create an employee and make every delete fail
2. Run cleanup
expected: Cleanup retries, does not throw, and reports the employee as leaked for the next purge

scenario: Create ESS User With Enabled Status
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Select User Role ESS and Status Enabled
4. Pick the new employee, enter a username, password and confirm password
5. Click Save
6. Search the user list by that username
input: Self-created employee (unique random last name); generated username and password
expected: "Successfully Saved" toast appears; the list shows "(1) Record Found" with that username, role ESS, the employee's name, and status Enabled
notes: Employee created via the API; teardown deletes it and the user goes with it (verified live), so the user needs no cleanup of its own.

scenario: Create Admin User With Disabled Status
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Select User Role Admin and Status Disabled
4. Pick the new employee, enter a username, password and confirm password
5. Click Save
6. Search the user list by that username
input: Self-created employee; generated username and password
expected: "Successfully Saved" toast appears; the list shows that user with role Admin and status Disabled
notes: Creates an account with Admin privileges, but Disabled and with a random password. Teardown deletes the employee and the user goes with it (cascade verified live for an Admin-role, Disabled user). Written out in full rather than shared with TC_UCF_001, so each test reads on its own.

scenario: Add User Shows Required Field Errors When Form Is Blank
steps:
1. Log in
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Confirm no field shows a validation message yet
4. Leave every field empty and click Save
5. Check each field's message
6. Check the page is still the Add User form and no success toast appeared
expected: User Role, Employee Name, Status, Username and Password each show "Required"; Confirm Password shows "Passwords do not match" (verified live - not "Required"). The page stays on the Add User form and no success toast appears (nothing was saved).
notes: Creates no data, so nothing to clean up (a manual probe also saw no create request; the test itself checks the URL and toast, not network traffic). Verified live before automating; the plan's assumption that Confirm Password says "Required" was wrong. One poll-based assertion over a field -> message object, so a failure names the field. The Confirm Password wording looks odd for an empty field (possible app quirk) - asserted as observed; if the app changes it the test fails on purpose for a person to decide.

scenario: Password And Confirm Password Mismatch Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create a new employee in PIM
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly, but enter a different value in Confirm Password
4. Click Save
input: Self-created employee; generated username; two different passwords
expected: A validation error appears on Confirm Password and no user is created. Exact message to be verified live before automating.
notes: Planned, not automated yet. Confirmed live already: a password with no digit is rejected ("Your password must contain minimum 1 number", see TC_CEF_003). Still to verify: minimum length and any other rules.

scenario: Username Shorter Than Minimum Length Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create a new employee in PIM
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly, but enter a username below the minimum length
4. Click Save
input: Self-created employee; a 4-character username (minimum length to be confirmed live)
expected: A validation error about the username length appears and no user is created. Exact limit and message to be verified live before automating.
notes: Planned, not automated yet. Boundary-style case; verify the actual minimum (and maximum) username length live first - no limit is assumed anywhere in the code.

scenario: Duplicate Username Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create two new employees in PIM
2. Create a user for the first employee
3. Open Add User again for the second employee and enter the same username
4. Click Save
input: Two self-created employees; one generated username used twice
expected: A validation error says the username is already taken and the second user is not created. Exact message to be verified live before automating.
notes: Planned, not automated yet. Needs two employees and one saved user as setup (create via the API); teardown removes both employees and their users.

scenario: Cancel Add User Returns To User List
steps:
1. Log in
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Click Cancel
expected: User is returned to the User Management list and no user is created. Exact URL to be verified live before automating.
notes: Planned, not automated yet. Creates no data.
